newsitem.title: USA: Poco sees big gains after Gardiner deal.
newsitem.headline: Poco sees big gains after Gardiner deal.

text.p: Poco Petroleums Ltd, which won shareholder approval on Wednesday for its C$230 million friendly takeover of Gardiner Oil & Gas, expects major increases in production and financial results in 1996 and 1997, Poco chief executive Craig Stewart said on Thursday.

Poco, which made the Gardiner acquisition because the target firm controlled key operating areas within Poco's main drilling region in Alberta, should produce an average 34,000 barrels per day of oil and gas liquids in 1996 and over 40,000 in 1997, Stewart told a FirstEnergy Capital Corp-Merrill Lynch & Co investment symposium.
Poco produced an average of just over 20,000 barrels per day in 1995.
He also said the company was set for average gas output of 295 million cubic feet per day this year and 450 million cubic feet per day next year, up from just over 200 million in 1995.
Cash flow per share was on target to hit C$1.78 on a fully diluted basis in 1996 and C$2.12 in 1997, Stewart said. Basic net earnings were projected at C$0.18 per share this year and next, he said.
Poco set its 1997 expenditure budget at C$300 million, down from C$685 million in 1996, Stewart said.
He said 95 percent of the properties acquired in the Gardiner purchase were in Poco's key Western Operating Region in north-central Alberta.
Poco has already identified 35 locations in the Gardiner lands for 1997 drilling and the properties were projected to contribute C$40 million to Poco's 1997 cash flow, Stewart said.
